newsitem.title: USA: Aberdeen soldier found not guilty of sex misconduct.
newsitem.headline: Aberdeen soldier found not guilty of sex misconduct.

text.p: One of eight soldiers charged in a U.S. Army sexual harassment scandal has been found not guilty of sexual misconduct in an administrative proceeding, an army spokesman said on Saturday.

However, Staff Sgt. Nathanael Beach, 32, was found guilty on Friday of charges of abuse of authority and failure to obey an order, said Ed Starnes, a spokesman for the Aberdeen Proving Ground Ordinance Centre and School.
Beach will be removed from a military promotion list and he also received a suspended penalty of forteiture of pay and allowances, Starnes said.
The guilty verdicts were being appealed, the spokesman added.

The verdict came a day after the highest ranking soldier charged in the scandal, Capt. Derrick Robertson, was convicted of consensual sex with a female trainee. A military judge sentenced him to three years in prison, dismissal from the service and forfeiture of all pay and allowance.
Because of a plea agreement reached hours before a pre-trial hearing was to begin, however, the prison sentence was reduced to one year, with all but four months suspended.

Starnes said the abuse of authority charge against Beach related to his requiring a woman trainee to type a class paper for him, and the failure to obey an order charge related to his discussing the case with the woman involved.
Starnes said the military usually would not discuss details of an administrative case until the appeals process was completed, but Beach's attorneys had gone public with the verdict.
